powerStructure.en: The United States operates as a constitutional presidential republic in which executive and legislative power are separately elected and may be held by different parties; unified or divided government is a standard analytic variable [constitution-article-2]. President Donald J. Trump (Republican) won the November 2024 election and was inaugurated on 20 January 2025, securing the executive branch for a second non-consecutive term [vdem-democracy-report-2026]. The government is UNIFIED: the Republican Party controls the presidency and both chambers of Congress simultaneously as of the run date. Senate (119th Congress, 2025-2027): Republicans hold 53 seats, Democrats 45 seats, 2 Independents (both caucusing with Democrats); the Republican majority controls the chamber [senate-party-division]. House of Representatives (119th Congress): Republicans hold 218 seats, Democrats 212 seats, 1 Independent, with 4 vacancies (run-date composition reflects resignations of Rep. Eric Swalwell D-CA on 14 April 2026, Rep. Tony Gonzales R-TX on 14 April 2026, Rep. Sheila Cherfilus-McCormick D-FL on 21 April 2026, and the death of Rep. David Scott D-GA on 22 April 2026); the Republican majority, though historically narrow, controls the chamber [house-party-breakdown]. The President, as commander-in-chief under Article II, controls the armed forces; the Secretary of Defense serves at the President's pleasure [constitution-article-2]. Judicial independence: federal judges, including Supreme Court justices, are appointed by the President with Senate confirmation and serve during 'good behaviour' (effectively life tenure); recent rulings have substantially expanded presidential removal power over executive-branch officers [trump-v-slaughter-2026][trump-v-cook-2026]. Media: the United States maintains formally independent private media operating under First Amendment protections; Freedom House scored the United States 81 out of 100 in 2026, its lowest score since the survey's 100-point system began in 2002, noting declines in press freedom indicators [freedom-house-2026]. POWER LOCUS — UNRESOLVED: Constitutionally, the Constitution of the United States (1787, in force 4 March 1789) distributes power among three co-equal branches — Congress, President, and the Judiciary — with checks and balances [constitution-usa-1787]. Whether operative power tracks this constitutional design is actively contested; recent Supreme Court rulings have expanded presidential immunity from criminal prosecution (Trump v. United States, 603 U.S. 593 (2024)), eliminated for-cause removal protections for independent agency commissioners (Trump v. Slaughter, 609 U.S. ___ (2026)), and sharply constrained nationwide judicial injunctions (Trump v. CASA, Inc., 606 U.S. 831 (2025)) — all of which structurally advantage the executive branch. The constitutional text distributes power; whether the operative locus tracks it is a judgment field that cannot be resolved by lookup alone [vdem-democracy-report-2026][pew-democracy-decline-2026].
powerStructure.fr: Les États-Unis fonctionnent comme une république présidentielle constitutionnelle dans laquelle les pouvoirs exécutif et législatif sont élus séparément et peuvent être détenus par des partis différents [constitution-article-2]. Le président Donald J. Trump (Républicain) a remporté l'élection de novembre 2024 et a été inauguré le 20 janvier 2025 [vdem-democracy-report-2026]. Le gouvernement est UNIFIÉ : le Parti républicain contrôle simultanément la présidence et les deux chambres du Congrès. Sénat (119e Congrès, 2025-2027) : 53 Républicains, 45 Démocrates, 2 Indépendants [senate-party-division]. Chambre des représentants : 218 Républicains, 212 Démocrates, 1 Indépendant, 4 vacances [house-party-breakdown]. Médias : Freedom House a noté les États-Unis 81 sur 100 en 2026, son score le plus bas depuis 2002 [freedom-house-2026]. POUVOIR OPÉRATIONNEL — NON RÉSOLU : la Constitution des États-Unis (1787) distribue le pouvoir entre trois branches coégales; la question de savoir si le pouvoir opérationnel suit cette conception est activement contestée; les décisions récentes de la Cour suprême ont élargi l'immunité présidentielle et les pouvoirs exécutifs au détriment des agences indépendantes et de la portée des injonctions judiciaires [vdem-democracy-report-2026][pew-democracy-decline-2026].

stabilityDrivers.en: Legitimacy derives primarily from electoral procedure: the United States holds regular, competitive elections at federal, state, and local levels; however, the Varieties of Democracy (V-Dem) Institute's Democracy Report 2026 recorded a 24 percent decline in the V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index score — from 0.75 in 2024 to 0.57 in 2025, the lowest since 1965 — characterized as 'much faster deterioration than at any point in the past 50 years' [vdem-democracy-report-2026][pew-democracy-decline-2026]. Armed forces loyalty: the U.S. military is constitutionally and institutionally subordinate to civilian elected authority; no credible evidence of institutional defection exists, though civil-military tensions over domestic deployment have emerged [dhs-hta-2025][acled-usa-july-2026]. Business elite alignment: the current administration has pursued deregulation and corporate tax maintenance aligned with large-capital interests; tariff policy has introduced uncertainty in manufacturing and retail supply chains, creating partial elite-business divergence on trade [ustr-trade-policy-2025][fed-monetary-policy-report-july-2026].
stabilityDrivers.fr: La légitimité découle principalement de la procédure électorale; le Democracy Report 2026 de l'Institut V-Dem a enregistré un déclin de 24 % du score de l'Indice de démocratie libérale — passant de 0,75 en 2024 à 0,57 en 2025, le plus bas depuis 1965 [vdem-democracy-report-2026][pew-democracy-decline-2026]. Loyauté des forces armées : les forces armées américaines sont constitutionnellement subordonnées à l'autorité civile élue; aucune preuve crédible de défection institutionnelle n'existe [dhs-hta-2025][acled-usa-july-2026]. La politique tarifaire de l'administration actuelle a introduit une incertitude dans les chaînes d'approvisionnement, créant une divergence partielle entre élites d'affaires et administration sur le commerce [ustr-trade-policy-2025][fed-monetary-policy-report-july-2026].

constitutionalSubstrate.en: The United States is a federal constitutional republic in which sovereignty is distributed between a central national government and 50 constituent states under a written constitution, with a presidential executive not derived from the legislature and a common-law legal tradition (Louisiana retaining civil law for private matters) [constitution-usa-1787]. SUBSTRATE STATUS: IN MOTION. The deep legal architecture comprises four distinct and separately held orders: (1) FEDERAL STATUTORY ORDER — supreme over state law by the Supremacy Clause (Article VI); grounded in the Constitution of the United States (1787, in force 4 March 1789); re-founded by the Reconstruction Amendments: Thirteenth Amendment (1865), Fourteenth Amendment (1868), Fifteenth Amendment (1870), which abolished chattel slavery, established birthright citizenship and equal protection, and prohibited race-based disenfranchisement [reconstruction-amendments]; judicial review established by Marbury v. Madison, 5 U.S. (1 Cranch) 137 (1803) [marbury-v-madison-1803]. (2) STATE STATUTORY AND COMMON LAW ORDER — each of the 50 states maintains its own legal system, legislature, and courts, operating concurrently with federal law within constitutional limits; Louisiana retains a civil-law tradition for private law matters [constitution-usa-1787]. (3) TRIBAL SOVEREIGN ORDER — federally recognized Indian tribes exercise inherent pre-constitutional sovereignty over their members and Indian country territory (as defined in 18 U.S.C. § 1151) under United States Code, Title 25 (Indians) — Federal Indian Law statutory corpus; sovereignty is not derived from federal or state law but is subject to congressional plenary power, established by The Marshall Trilogy — Johnson v. M'Intosh (1823), Cherokee Nation v. Georgia (1831), Worcester v. Georgia (1832); reinforced by Haaland v. Brackeen, 599 U.S. 255 (2023); jurisdiction reallocated by McGirt v. Oklahoma, 591 U.S. 894 (2020) and partially reversed by Oklahoma v. Castro-Huerta, 597 U.S. 629 (2022) [marshall-trilogy][usc-title-25][haaland-v-brackeen-2023][mcgirt-v-oklahoma-2020][oklahoma-v-castro-huerta-2022]. (4) INSULAR TERRITORIAL ORDER — the five inhabited unincorporated territories (Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; Guam; United States Virgin Islands (USVI); Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI); American Samoa) are governed under a distinct constitutional regime established by The Insular Cases — De Lima v. Bidwell, 182 U.S. 1 (1901); Downes v. Bidwell, 182 U.S. 244 (1901) — under which Congress has plenary authority and the Constitution applies only selectively; residents hold no presidential voting rights [insular-cases-1901][doi-insular-affairs]. ACTIVE REALLOCATION IN MOTION — present-state facts, not future trajectory: Loper Bright Enterprises v. Raimondo, 603 U.S. 369 (2024) overruled Chevron deference; Trump v. United States, 603 U.S. 593 (2024) established absolute presidential immunity for core constitutional acts; Trump v. CASA, Inc., 606 U.S. 831 (2025) held that nationwide injunctions likely exceed federal judicial equity power; West Virginia v. Environmental Protection Agency (EPA), 597 U.S. 697 (2022) established the major questions doctrine; Trump v. Slaughter, 609 U.S. ___ (2026) overruled Humphrey's Executor (1935), eliminating for-cause removal protections for Federal Trade Commission commissioners; Trump v. Cook, 609 U.S. ___ (2026) held the Federal Reserve's distinct historical tradition shields it from at-will removal; Trump v. Barbara, 609 U.S. ___ (2026) struck down Executive Order 14160 and affirmed birthright citizenship under the Fourteenth Amendment extends to children born to parents unlawfully or temporarily present; Watson v. Republican National Committee, 609 U.S. ___ (2026) clarified federal-versus-state allocation in election administration [loper-bright-2024][trump-v-usa-2024][trump-v-casa-2025][wv-v-epa-2022][trump-v-slaughter-2026][trump-v-cook-2026][trump-v-barbara-2026][watson-v-rnc-2026][crs-congress-gov].
constitutionalSubstrate.fr: Les États-Unis constituent une république constitutionnelle fédérale dans laquelle la souveraineté est distribuée entre un gouvernement national central et 50 États constituants, avec un exécutif présidentiel non issu du législatif et une tradition juridique de common law [constitution-usa-1787]. STATUT DU SUBSTRAT : EN MOUVEMENT. L'architecture juridique profonde comprend quatre ordres distincts et séparément maintenus : (1) L'ORDRE STATUTAIRE FÉDÉRAL — suprême sur le droit des États par la Clause de suprématie (Article VI); fondé sur la Constitution de 1787; refondé par les Amendements de la Reconstruction (Treizième, Quatorzième, Quinzième Amendements, 1865-1870) qui ont aboli l'esclavage, établi la citoyenneté par naissance et la protection égale [reconstruction-amendments]; contrôle judiciaire établi par Marbury v. Madison (1803) [marbury-v-madison-1803]. (2) L'ORDRE STATUTAIRE ET DE COMMON LAW DES ÉTATS — chacun des 50 États maintient son propre système juridique [constitution-usa-1787]. (3) L'ORDRE DE SOUVERAINETÉ TRIBALE — souveraineté inhérente pré-constitutionnelle des tribus reconnues sur leurs membres et le territoire de l'Indian country; établi par The Marshall Trilogy (1823-1832); réaffirmé par Haaland v. Brackeen (2023); réalloué partiellement par McGirt v. Oklahoma (2020) et Oklahoma v. Castro-Huerta (2022) [marshall-trilogy][usc-title-25][haaland-v-brackeen-2023][mcgirt-v-oklahoma-2020][oklahoma-v-castro-huerta-2022]. (4) L'ORDRE TERRITORIAL INSULAIRE — cinq territoires non incorporés habités régis par les Insular Cases (1901) [insular-cases-1901][doi-insular-affairs]. RÉALLOCATION ACTIVE EN COURS : Loper Bright (2024), Trump v. United States (2024), Trump v. CASA (2025), West Virginia v. EPA (2022), Trump v. Slaughter (2026), Trump v. Cook (2026), Trump v. Barbara (2026), Watson v. RNC (2026) constituent des faits d'état présent réallouant activement les pouvoirs [loper-bright-2024][trump-v-usa-2024][trump-v-casa-2025][wv-v-epa-2022][trump-v-slaughter-2026][trump-v-cook-2026][trump-v-barbara-2026][watson-v-rnc-2026][crs-congress-gov].

macroReality.en: The United States economy is the world's largest by nominal gross domestic product (GDP), driven predominantly by services — finance, technology, healthcare, professional services — with manufacturing and agriculture as significant secondary sectors rather than the primary base. Real GDP grew at an annualized rate of 2.1 percent in the first quarter (Q1) of 2026 (third estimate), revised upward from 1.6 percent in the second estimate, following 0.5 percent growth in Q4 2025; growth in Q1 2026 reflected increases in real value added of 7.5 percent for government, 4.5 percent for private goods-producing industries, and 0.8 percent for private services-producing industries [bea-gdp-q1-2026]. The International Monetary Fund (IMF) World Economic Outlook Update, July 2026 projects full-year 2026 U.S. GDP growth at 2.3 percent — the fastest among major advanced economies — and 2.2 percent in 2027 [imf-weo-july-2026]. Inflation: the Consumer Price Index for All Urban Consumers (CPI-U) rose 4.2 percent on a twelve-month basis through May 2026, the fastest rate in three years; monthly increase was 0.5 percent in May following 0.6 percent in April; core CPI (excluding food and energy) rose 2.9 percent year-over-year, driven significantly by a 23.5 percent twelve-month surge in energy prices [bls-cpi-may-2026]. Monetary policy: the Federal Reserve (Fed), as reported in the Monetary Policy Report, July 2026 submitted to Congress, is maintaining an extended pause on rate adjustments, signalling a 'higher for longer' stance given inflation persistence above target [fed-monetary-policy-report-july-2026]. Fiscal position: the federal deficit in fiscal year (FY) 2025 totalled approximately $1.8 trillion ($5.2 trillion in revenues, $7.0 trillion in outlays); the Congressional Budget Office (CBO) estimated the FY 2026 deficit is tracking above FY 2025 totals, with $1.4 trillion borrowed in the first nine months of FY 2026 [cbo-budget-fy2025]. Federal debt: the U.S. Government Financial Report FY 2025 placed the federal debt-to-GDP ratio at 99 percent at end of FY 2025 (September 30, 2025) under the Treasury's own accounting; total public debt as measured by the Federal Reserve reached approximately 122.6 percent of GDP in Q4 2025 under a broader measure inclusive of intragovernmental holdings [treasury-debt-gdp-fy2025]. Credit rating: Moody's Ratings Downgrades United States Ratings to Aa1 from Aaa; Changes Outlook to Stable in May 2025, the last of the three major agencies to downgrade, leaving the U.S. rated AA+/AA+/Aa1 (Standard & Poor's, Fitch, Moody's) [moodys-downgrade-2025].
macroReality.fr: L'économie des États-Unis est la plus grande du monde par produit intérieur brut (PIB) nominal, principalement portée par les services — finance, technologie, santé, services professionnels. Le PIB réel a progressé à un taux annualisé de 2,1 % au T1 2026 (troisième estimation); le FMI projette 2,3 % pour l'ensemble de 2026 — la plus rapide parmi les grandes économies avancées [bea-gdp-q1-2026][imf-weo-july-2026]. Inflation : l'Indice des prix à la consommation pour l'ensemble des consommateurs urbains (CPI-U) a augmenté de 4,2 % sur douze mois jusqu'en mai 2026, porté par une hausse de 23,5 % des prix de l'énergie [bls-cpi-may-2026]. Politique monétaire : la Réserve fédérale maintient une pause prolongée sur les ajustements de taux, signalant une posture 'plus élevé plus longtemps' [fed-monetary-policy-report-july-2026]. Position budgétaire : déficit d'environ 1 800 milliards de dollars en EF 2025; ratio dette/PIB fédéral à 99 % fin EF 2025 ou ~122,6 % selon une mesure plus large [cbo-budget-fy2025][treasury-debt-gdp-fy2025]. Note de crédit : Moody's a déclassé à Aa1 depuis Aaa en mai 2025 [moodys-downgrade-2025].

externalVulnerability.en: For full-year 2025, U.S. goods and services exports totalled $3,432.3 billion and imports $4,333.8 billion, yielding a goods-and-services deficit of $901.5 billion — down $2.1 billion from 2024 and among the largest goods trade deficits of any country [bea-trade-annual-2025]. On a rolling twelve-month basis through May 2026, the total U.S. trade deficit was $728.0 billion [census-foreign-trade-press-release-2026]. The trade deficit is structurally driven by goods: the United States runs surpluses in services trade but large deficits in manufactured goods. Top goods trading partners by volume include Canada, Mexico, China, Germany, and Japan; the U.S.-Mexico-Canada Agreement (USMCA) governs the North American trade relationship [ustr-trade-policy-2025]. Sovereign debt: federal debt at approximately 99 percent of GDP as of 30 September 2025; the Federal Reserve's Distributional Financial Accounts show foreign holders owning approximately one-quarter to one-third of publicly held Treasury securities, with Japan and China as the largest foreign sovereign holders [treasury-debt-gdp-fy2025][fed-dfa]. International Monetary Fund program status: no program; the United States is an Article IV member subject to annual surveillance but holds no conditionality arrangement. Sanctions: the United States is the world's primary sanctions-imposing state, not a target of multilateral sanctions [ustr-trade-policy-2025].
externalVulnerability.fr: Pour l'année complète 2025, le déficit biens-et-services des États-Unis était de 901,5 milliards de dollars [bea-trade-annual-2025]; sur les douze mois glissants jusqu'en mai 2026, de 728,0 milliards de dollars [census-foreign-trade-press-release-2026]. Les principaux partenaires commerciaux comprennent le Canada, le Mexique, la Chine, l'Allemagne et le Japon; l'Accord États-Unis-Mexique-Canada (AEUMC) régit la relation commerciale nord-américaine [ustr-trade-policy-2025]. Les détenteurs étrangers possèdent environ un quart à un tiers des titres du Trésor publiquement détenus, avec le Japon et la Chine comme principaux détenteurs souverains étrangers [treasury-debt-gdp-fy2025][fed-dfa]. Statut Programme du FMI : aucun programme [ustr-trade-policy-2025].

politicalEconomy.en: The current economic model disproportionately benefits the owners of financial and technology capital: the Federal Reserve's Distributional Financial Accounts show that the top 1 percent of U.S. households holds approximately 30 percent of total U.S. household wealth, and the top 10 percent holds approximately 67 percent, while the bottom 50 percent holds approximately 3 percent [fed-dfa]. The business elite structure is concentrated in technology (large-cap platform firms), finance, defense, and energy. Reforms that are technically necessary — fiscal consolidation to address the long-run debt trajectory projected by the U.S. Government Financial Report FY 2025 to reach 576 percent of GDP by 2100 under current policy; healthcare cost containment; labour-market adaptation for artificial intelligence (AI) displacement; and climate transition investment — are politically constrained: the narrow House majority makes multi-year fiscal legislation structurally difficult, and sectoral interests in fossil fuels and healthcare are well-positioned to resist cost-bearing reforms [treasury-debt-gdp-fy2025][moodys-downgrade-2025][house-party-breakdown].
politicalEconomy.fr: Le modèle économique actuel bénéficie de manière disproportionnée aux propriétaires de capital financier et technologique : les Distributional Financial Accounts de la Réserve fédérale montrent que le 1 % supérieur détient environ 30 % de la richesse totale des ménages, et le 10 % supérieur environ 67 %, tandis que les 50 % inférieurs en détiennent environ 3 % [fed-dfa]. Les réformes techniquement nécessaires — consolidation budgétaire, maîtrise des coûts de santé, adaptation à l'intelligence artificielle (IA), investissement dans la transition climatique — sont politiquement contraintes par la majorité étroite à la Chambre et les intérêts sectoriels bien organisés [treasury-debt-gdp-fy2025][moodys-downgrade-2025][house-party-breakdown].

geography.en: The United States is a continental coastal state stretching from the Atlantic to the Pacific Ocean, sharing land borders with Canada to the north and Mexico to the south, with non-contiguous states in Alaska (bordering Canada and Russia across the Bering Strait) and the Hawaiian archipelago in the central Pacific, plus five inhabited insular territories spread across the Pacific and Caribbean [doi-insular-affairs]. Land area of the 50 states and the District of Columbia totals approximately 9.83 million square kilometres; internal distances are continental — roughly 4,500 km coast-to-coast. The Bureau of Transportation Statistics Transportation Statistics Annual Report 2025 records the contiguous United States with approximately 12,400 miles of general coastline; the NOAA Office for Coastal Management data reports that approximately 40 percent of the U.S. population lives in coastal counties, generating over $9 trillion in GDP annually [bts-tsar-2025][noaa-coastal-management-fastfacts]. The Federal Communications Commission (FCC) Broadband Data Collection — December 2024 Data shows broadband available to approximately 97 percent of the U.S. population at fixed locations, though approximately 22 million Americans lack access to fixed broadband meeting FCC speed thresholds [fcc-broadband-data-collection]. The periphery — Commonwealth of Puerto Rico; Guam; United States Virgin Islands (USVI); Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands (CNMI); American Samoa — is administered by the Office of Insular Affairs (OIA), U.S. Department of the Interior [doi-insular-affairs].
geography.fr: Les États-Unis sont un État côtier continental s'étendant de l'océan Atlantique à l'océan Pacifique, partageant des frontières terrestres avec le Canada au nord et le Mexique au sud, avec des États non contigus en Alaska et l'archipel hawaïen, plus cinq territoires insulaires habités répartis dans le Pacifique et les Caraïbes [doi-insular-affairs]. La superficie terrestre totale est d'environ 9,83 millions de km²; les distances intérieures sont continentales, d'environ 4 500 km d'une côte à l'autre. Environ 40 % de la population américaine vit dans les comtés côtiers, générant plus de 9 000 milliards de dollars de PIB annuellement [bts-tsar-2025][noaa-coastal-management-fastfacts]. Le haut débit est disponible pour environ 97 % de la population aux emplacements fixes, bien qu'environ 22 millions d'Américains manquent encore d'accès [fcc-broadband-data-collection]. La périphérie insulaire est administrée par le Bureau des affaires insulaires (OIA) du Département de l'Intérieur américain [doi-insular-affairs].

minerals.en: The United States holds substantial critical-mineral endowments across a wide range of commodities, as documented in the Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025 published by the U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). Key reserves and resources (USGS 2025 estimates): copper reserves of approximately 51 million metric tons (mmt) — fourth-largest globally; gold reserves of approximately 3,000 metric tons; coal resources among the largest globally; lithium resources estimated at approximately 12 million mt of lithium content, primarily in brine and clay deposits in Nevada and Arizona; rare earth element (REE) reserves of approximately 2.3 million mt — second globally after China; phosphate rock reserves of approximately 1 billion mt — second globally; helium reserves among the world's largest; copper, gold, and molybdenum are actively produced at scale; cobalt resources are present but production is limited [usgs-mcs-2025]. Strategic gap: the United States is import-dependent for many critical minerals on its own critical minerals list, including cobalt, manganese, niobium, and heavy REEs; dependence on Chinese processing and refining capacity for REEs and battery materials represents the principal strategic mineral vulnerability even where domestic ore resources exist [usgs-mcs-2025].
minerals.fr: Les États-Unis détiennent des dotations substantielles en minéraux critiques selon les Mineral Commodity Summaries 2025 du U.S. Geological Survey (USGS). Réserves et ressources clés (USGS 2025) : cuivre ~51 millions de tonnes métriques (Mt) (4e rang mondial); or ~3 000 tonnes métriques; ressources en charbon parmi les plus importantes au monde; lithium ~12 millions de Mt de contenu, principalement dans les dépôts du Nevada et de l'Arizona; éléments de terres rares (ETR) ~2,3 millions de Mt (2e rang mondial après la Chine); roche phosphatée ~1 milliard de Mt (2e rang mondial) [usgs-mcs-2025]. Lacune stratégique : les États-Unis sont importateurs dépendants pour le cobalt, le manganèse, le niobium et les ETR lourds; la dépendance à la capacité chinoise de transformation des ETR et des matériaux de batteries représente la principale vulnérabilité minérale stratégique [usgs-mcs-2025].

biosphere.en: Forests: the Global Forest Resources Assessment 2025 published by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO) documents U.S. forest area at approximately 310 million hectares — roughly one-third of the country's land area — with a net positive forest area trend due to reforestation in the eastern United States offsetting western losses from wildfire; wildfire-driven degradation in the western states represents an accelerating structural loss [fao-fra-2025]. Freshwater: the AQUASTAT Country Profile — United States of America published by the FAO shows total renewable freshwater resources of approximately 3,069 km3 per year; however, water stress is acute and worsening in the arid and semi-arid West, including the Colorado River Basin and Ogallala (High Plains) Aquifer, which is being drawn down faster than recharge — a structural depletion with no near-term solution [fao-aquastat-usa]. Arable land: the 2022 Census of Agriculture: Farms and Farmland Highlights published by the USDA National Agricultural Statistics Service (NASS) shows approximately 893 million acres in farms, of which approximately 315 million acres are cropland; farmland has declined from a 1954 peak in area but productivity per acre has increased substantially [usda-nass-census-agriculture-2022]. Fisheries: the Status of Stocks Reports — Annual Report to Congress on the Status of U.S. Fisheries published by NOAA Fisheries (2024 report, covering stocks through 2023) shows that of 220 stocks with known status, 85 percent are not subject to overfishing and 76 percent are not overfished [noaa-status-stocks-2024].
biosphere.fr: Forêts : l'Évaluation des ressources forestières mondiales 2025 de la FAO documente une superficie forestière américaine d'environ 310 millions d'hectares, avec une tendance nette positive due à la reforestation dans l'est [fao-fra-2025]. Eau douce : le profil de pays AQUASTAT de la FAO montre des ressources en eau douce renouvelable totales d'environ 3 069 km3 par an; le stress hydrique est aigu dans l'Ouest aride, notamment dans le bassin du Colorado et l'aquifère Ogallala (nappe des Hautes Plaines) [fao-aquastat-usa]. Terres arables : le recensement agricole 2022 du NASS du USDA montre environ 893 millions d'acres dans des exploitations, dont environ 315 millions d'acres de terres cultivées [usda-nass-census-agriculture-2022]. Pêcheries : le rapport annuel Status of Stocks Reports de NOAA Fisheries (2024) montre que 85 % des 220 stocks à statut connu ne sont pas soumis à la surpêche et que 76 % ne sont pas surexploités [noaa-status-stocks-2024].

climate.en: The United States spans an extraordinarily diverse range of climate types — from Arctic tundra in Alaska to tropical rainforest in Hawaii, humid subtropical in the Southeast, semi-arid and arid in the interior West, Mediterranean in coastal California, and temperate continental across the Midwest and Northeast — making it among the most climatically heterogeneous countries on Earth. The Fifth National Climate Assessment (NCA5) published by the U.S. Global Change Research Program (USGCRP) in 2023 documents that observed warming across the contiguous United States has averaged approximately 1.6 degrees Fahrenheit (0.9 degrees Celsius) above a 1901-1960 baseline, with the fastest warming in Alaska (up to 4 degrees Fahrenheit above a 1925-1975 baseline) [nca5]. Principal hazards by region: SOUTHEAST AND SOUTH CENTRAL — extreme heat, drought, and flooding; days above 95 degrees Fahrenheit projected (under high-emissions scenarios, SSP5-8.5, through 2100) to increase by up to 49 days in southern regions [nca5]. WEST — wildfire: burned area has increased dramatically and is projected to increase further under all emissions scenarios; drought stress on the Colorado River system is acute [nca5]. COASTS (Atlantic and Gulf) — sea-level rise: NCA5 projects 0.3-0.7 metres of mean sea-level rise by 2100 under a low-emissions scenario (Shared Socioeconomic Pathway (SSP)2-4.5) and 0.5-1.2 metres under a high-emissions scenario (SSP5-8.5); storm surge risk concentrated in Gulf Coast and Atlantic coastline [nca5][noaa-coastal-management-fastfacts]. GREAT PLAINS — drought and precipitation variability threaten the Ogallala Aquifer system [nca5]. Adaptive capacity: the Notre Dame Global Adaptation Initiative (ND-GAIN) Country Index ranks the United States among the highest-readiness countries globally; however, this aggregate masks sharp internal disparities — low-income communities in the Gulf South, urban heat islands in inland cities, and tribal nations in the Southwest face exposures that exceed their adaptive resources [nd-gain-country-index].
climate.fr: Les États-Unis couvrent une gamme extraordinairement diverse de types climatiques — de la toundra arctique en Alaska à la forêt tropicale humide à Hawaï, subtropicale humide dans le Sud-Est, semi-aride et aride dans l'Ouest intérieur, méditerranéen sur la côte californienne, et tempéré continental dans le Midwest et le Nord-Est. Le Fifth National Climate Assessment (NCA5) du U.S. Global Change Research Program (USGCRP) (2023) documente un réchauffement observé d'environ 1,6 degré Fahrenheit (0,9 degré Celsius) au-dessus d'une référence 1901-1960 [nca5]. Principaux aléas par région : SUD-EST — chaleur extrême, sécheresse et inondations; jours dépassant 95 degrés Fahrenheit projetés en hausse jusqu'à 49 jours dans les régions méridionales sous SSP5-8.5 [nca5]. OUEST — incendies de forêt et sécheresse accentuée [nca5]. CÔTES — élévation du niveau de la mer : 0,3-0,7 m d'ici 2100 sous SSP2-4.5 et 0,5-1,2 m sous SSP5-8.5 [nca5][noaa-coastal-management-fastfacts]. L'Indice ND-GAIN classe les États-Unis parmi les pays à plus haute capacité d'adaptation mondiale, avec des disparités internes marquées pour les communautés à faibles revenus et les nations tribales [nd-gain-country-index].

metabolism.en: Energy: the United States is a net energy exporter — a position it has held since 2019. In 2025, total energy exports reached a record 31 quadrillion British thermal units (quads), up 2 percent year-over-year, while imports fell 5 percent to 21 quads, yielding record net exports of 11 quads, 20 percent above the prior record [eia-steo-july-2026]. The United States Energy Information Administration (EIA) Annual Energy Outlook 2026 projects the U.S. remaining a net energy exporter through 2050 in the reference case; crude oil production reached approximately 13.6 million barrels per day (bpd) in mid-2025, a record level; the U.S. is the world's largest natural gas producer [eia-aeo-2026][eia-steo-july-2026]. Food: the United States is a substantial net food exporter; however, the Household Food Security in the United States in 2024 published by the USDA Economic Research Service (ERS) shows that approximately 13-14 percent of U.S. households are food insecure in any given year, concentrated among households with low income, children, and in the South — the distribution network and price system, not aggregate production, is the binding constraint [usda-ers-food-security-2024]. Water: aggregate renewable freshwater resources are large but regionally misallocated; the Western United States faces structural water stress from over-allocation, aquifer depletion, and reduced snowpack that aggregate sufficiency figures mask [fao-aquastat-usa].
metabolism.fr: Énergie : les États-Unis sont exportateurs nets d'énergie depuis 2019. En 2025, les exportations totales d'énergie ont atteint un record de 31 quads, dégageant des exportations nettes record de 11 quads [eia-steo-july-2026]. L'Annual Energy Outlook 2026 de la U.S. Energy Information Administration (EIA) projette les États-Unis comme exportateurs nets d'énergie jusqu'en 2050; la production de pétrole brut a atteint environ 13,6 millions de barils par jour (bpj) à mi-2025 [eia-aeo-2026][eia-steo-july-2026]. Alimentation : les États-Unis sont exportateurs nets importants; cependant, environ 13-14 % des ménages américains sont en situation d'insécurité alimentaire, le réseau de distribution et le système de prix, et non la production aggregate, étant la contrainte contraignante [usda-ers-food-security-2024]. Eau : stress structurel hydrique dans l'Ouest américain dû à la sur-allocation et à l'épuisement des aquifères [fao-aquastat-usa].

transition.en: The United States is rated Critically Insufficient by the Climate Action Tracker (CAT); the CAT's USA — Climate Action Tracker (June 2026 update) documents that the Trump administration has withdrawn the United States from the Paris Agreement (annulling Biden administration 2030, 2035, and 2050 emissions reduction targets), revoked key power sector and transport sector emissions regulations, moved to eliminate the Environmental Protection Agency's (EPA's) legal authority to regulate greenhouse gas emissions, and invoked emergency powers to expand oil and gas drilling — constituting 'the most aggressive, comprehensive, and consequential climate policy rollback that the Climate Action Tracker has ever analysed' [cat-usa-2026]. Under current policies, U.S. emissions are projected by CAT to decline only 19-30 percent below 2005 levels by 2030 (excluding land use, land-use change, and forestry (LULUCF)), compared to the 29-39 percent trajectory under Biden-era policies; emissions would be 600-800 million tonnes of CO2 equivalent (MtCO2e) higher in 2030 than under the prior administration's path [cat-usa-2026]. The One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB) undermines the Inflation Reduction Act (IRA) deployment incentives for renewable energy and clean energy technologies [cat-usa-2026]. Observed trajectory: U.S. energy-related carbon dioxide (CO2) emissions decreased by 0.5 percent in 2024, per the CO2 Emissions — Global Energy Review 2025 of the International Energy Agency (IEA) — a marginal reduction driven by natural gas displacing coal and renewable growth [iea-co2-review-2025]. The U.S. has abandoned its net-zero target; CAT evaluates the net-zero target as 'No target' as of June 2026 [cat-usa-2026]. The Statistical Review of World Energy 2026 published by the Energy Institute confirms that while renewable energy capacity has continued to grow driven by market economics, the U.S. emissions trajectory has decoupled from what a 1.5-degree-Celsius-aligned path would require [energy-institute-stat-review-2026].
transition.fr: Les États-Unis sont classés Nettement insuffisant par le Climate Action Tracker (CAT); le CAT — USA — Climate Action Tracker (mise à jour de juin 2026) documente que l'administration Trump a retiré les États-Unis de l'Accord de Paris, révoqué les réglementations d'émissions clés, et invoqué des pouvoirs d'urgence pour étendre le forage pétrolier et gazier — constituant 'le retournement politique climatique le plus agressif, complet et conséquent que le Climate Action Tracker ait jamais analysé' [cat-usa-2026]. Sous les politiques actuelles, les émissions américaines sont projetées à une réduction de seulement 19-30 % en dessous des niveaux de 2005 d'ici 2030, soit 600-800 millions de tonnes d'équivalent CO2 (MtCO2e) de plus en 2030 que sous la trajectoire de l'administration précédente [cat-usa-2026]. Le One Big Beautiful Bill Act (OBBB) compromet les incitations de la Loi sur la réduction de l'inflation (IRA). Les émissions liées à l'énergie ont diminué de 0,5 % en 2024 selon la CO2 Emissions — Global Energy Review 2025 de l'Agence internationale de l'énergie (AIE) [iea-co2-review-2025]. Les États-Unis ont abandonné leur objectif de zéro émission net [cat-usa-2026].

permitting.en: Federal permitting for major infrastructure projects is tracked through the FAST-41 Permitting Dashboard operated by the Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (FPISC), established by Title 41 of the Fixing America's Surface Transportation Act (FAST-41, 42 U.S.C. § 4370m); as of run date, the dashboard tracks 87 active major federal infrastructure projects across energy, transportation, and mining sectors [permits-performance-gov]. The Council on Environmental Quality (CEQ) EIS Timelines Report: 2025 documents that the median time to complete a federal Environmental Impact Statement (EIS) under the National Environmental Policy Act (NEPA) has been approximately 3.5-4.5 years across agencies [ceq-eis-timelines-2025]. The Resources for the Future study National Environmental Policy Act Timelines and Outcomes for Clean Energy Projects (2025) finds that NEPA timelines for clean energy projects, while long, typically result in project approval rather than rejection [rff-nepa-timelines-clean-energy-2025]. State permitting: the Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory (LBNL) inventory Laws in Order (2024) covering all 50 states and Puerto Rico finds that siting authority for large-scale renewable energy facilities is held at different governmental levels across states, with defined timelines existing in only a minority of states [lbnl-state-siting-inventory-2024]. The binding constraint for power generation has shifted from land permitting to grid interconnection: the LBNL Queued Up: 2025 Edition documents approximately 2,600 gigawatts (GW) of generating capacity in interconnection queues as of end-2024 — over twice the current installed U.S. generating capacity — with median process duration of over four years and withdrawal rates exceeding 70 percent of queued capacity [lbnl-queued-up-2025]. The Frontiers in Sustainable Energy Policy study (2026) found that state-based renewable siting processes approved approximately 75 percent of projects that received formal review [frontiers-state-permitting-wind-solar-2026].
permitting.fr: Les autorisations fédérales pour les grands projets d'infrastructure sont suivies via le FAST-41 Permitting Dashboard du Federal Permitting Improvement Steering Council (FPISC); à la date de rédaction, le tableau de bord suit 87 projets d'infrastructure fédéraux majeurs actifs [permits-performance-gov]. Le CEQ EIS Timelines Report: 2025 documente que le délai médian pour compléter une étude d'impact environnemental (EIS) en vertu de la Loi sur la politique environnementale nationale (NEPA) est d'environ 3,5 à 4,5 ans [ceq-eis-timelines-2025]. La contrainte contraignante pour la production d'énergie s'est déplacée de l'autorisation foncière à l'interconnexion au réseau : le Queued Up: 2025 Edition du LBNL documente environ 2 600 gigawatts (GW) de capacité en file d'attente d'interconnexion fin 2024 — plus du double de la capacité installée actuelle — avec une durée médiane de traitement dépassant quatre ans et des taux de retrait dépassant 70 % [lbnl-queued-up-2025]. La permittisation des États est hautement variable, avec des délais définis dans une minorité d'États seulement [lbnl-state-siting-inventory-2024].

delivery.en: The Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), enacted in 2021, authorized and appropriated over $551 billion to the U.S. Department of Transportation (DOT) and other agencies for infrastructure delivery. The U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) report Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act: DOT Should Better Monitor Project Delivery and Spending (July 2025) found that as of April 2025, DOT had obligated 59 percent of its available IIJA funding and outlaid over half of that funding to recipients; GAO identified weaknesses in DOT's ability to track whether projects are on time and on budget [gao-iija-delivery-2025]. Infrastructure condition: the 2025 Report Card for America's Infrastructure published by the American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) assigned the United States an overall infrastructure grade of 'C' (mediocre, requiring attention) — the best grade since ASCE began grading in 1998 and an improvement from 'C-' in 2021; grades range from 'B' for ports to 'D' for stormwater, transit, and wastewater; nine of 18 categories remain within the 'D' range [asce-infra-2025]. Structural caveat: as a professional engineering organization, ASCE has an institutional interest in identifying infrastructure deficits; the direction of improvement is independently corroborated by IIJA funding flow data [asce-infra-2025][gao-iija-delivery-2025].
delivery.fr: La Infrastructure Investment and Jobs Act (IIJA), promulguée en 2021, a autorisé et approprié plus de 551 milliards de dollars au Département des transports américain (DOT). Le rapport du U.S. Government Accountability Office (GAO) (juillet 2025) a constaté qu'au 30 avril 2025, le DOT avait engagé 59 % de ses fonds IIJA disponibles, tout en identifiant des lacunes dans la surveillance de l'exécution des projets [gao-iija-delivery-2025]. Le 2025 Report Card for America's Infrastructure de l'American Society of Civil Engineers (ASCE) a attribué une note globale de 'C' (médiocre) — la meilleure note depuis 1998; neuf des 18 catégories restent dans la plage 'D' [asce-infra-2025].

productivity.en: Nonfarm business sector labor productivity increased 0.3 percent (quarter-over-quarter, annualized) in Q1 2026 (revised), down from 1.6 percent in Q4 2025, as output increased 2.0 percent and hours worked increased 1.3 percent; over the trailing four quarters, productivity growth has averaged approximately 1.0-1.5 percent — above the post-2007 average but below the pace consistent with AI-driven productivity acceleration at the scale projected by technology-sector advocates [bls-productivity-q1-2026]. The OECD Product Market Regulation Indicators — United States Country Note identifies professional licensing as a significant barrier to labour mobility between states — with over 1,100 distinct occupational licensing regimes across the 50 states creating friction in the movement of workers in healthcare, construction, and services [oecd-pmr-usa]. Interstate barriers to capital mobility are limited by the Commerce Clause of the Constitution, but regulatory divergence between states — particularly in environmental permitting, energy siting, and land-use regulation — creates material differences in the cost of doing business across states [oecd-pmr-usa].
productivity.fr: La productivité du travail dans le secteur non agricole a augmenté de 0,3 % (en rythme annualisé) au T1 2026 (révisé), en baisse depuis 1,6 % au T4 2025, la production ayant augmenté de 2,0 % et les heures travaillées de 1,3 % [bls-productivity-q1-2026]. Les Indicateurs de réglementation des marchés de produits de l'Organisation de coopération et de développement économiques (OCDE) identifient les licences professionnelles comme une barrière significative à la mobilité du travail entre États — avec plus de 1 100 régimes de licences professionnelles distincts à travers les 50 États [oecd-pmr-usa].

demographics.en: The United States is a settler-immigrant-built nation whose demographic character has been continuously shaped by successive waves of immigration since the colonial period, making migration the decisive variable in population dynamics. Total population: approximately 341.8 million as of 1 July 2025, per Vintage 2025 National and State Population Estimates published by the U.S. Census Bureau, representing an increase of approximately 1.8 million (0.5 percent) from 2024 — a significant deceleration from 2024's growth rate of approximately 1.0 percent [census-population-estimates-2025]. Age structure: the U.S. Census Bureau analysis U.S. Population Aging as Nation Turns 250 based on Vintage 2025 estimates documents a rising median age of approximately 39 years; the United States faces a less acute aging crisis than peer economies (Japan, Germany, South Korea) due to sustained immigration inflows and relatively higher fertility [census-age-sex-2025]. Net immigration in the year ending 1 July 2025 was approximately 1.3 million — a significant decline from 2.7 million in 2024 and 2.3 million in 2023, reflecting the impact of policy shifts under the current administration [census-population-estimates-2025]. The Congressional Budget Office (CBO) Demographic Outlook: 2025 to 2055 projects that under baseline assumptions, net immigration will remain the primary driver of long-run U.S. population growth; fertility is below replacement but above levels in most peer economies [cbo-demographic-outlook-2025]. Urban/rural split: approximately 80 percent of the U.S. population resides in metropolitan areas; rural population is older, less educated on average, and has experienced outmigration for decades, creating persistent rural-urban development disparities [census-population-estimates-2025].
demographics.fr: Les États-Unis sont une nation bâtie par des colons et des immigrants dont le caractère démographique a été continuellement façonné par des vagues successives d'immigration, faisant de la migration la variable déterminante de la dynamique démographique. Population totale : environ 341,8 millions au 1er juillet 2025, selon les Vintage 2025 National and State Population Estimates du U.S. Census Bureau, représentant une augmentation de 0,5 % par rapport à 2024 — une décélération significative [census-population-estimates-2025]. L'âge médian est d'environ 39 ans; les États-Unis présentent un vieillissement modéré moins aigu que le Japon ou l'Allemagne [census-age-sex-2025]. L'immigration nette dans l'année se terminant le 1er juillet 2025 était d'environ 1,3 million — en baisse depuis 2,7 millions en 2024 [census-population-estimates-2025]. Le Demographic Outlook: 2025 to 2055 du Congressional Budget Office (CBO) projette que l'immigration nette restera le principal moteur de la croissance démographique à long terme [cbo-demographic-outlook-2025].

composition.en: Ethnic and racial composition (Kaiser Family Foundation (KFF) tabulation of U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) data, 2024): White non-Hispanic approximately 59 percent; Hispanic or Latino approximately 19 percent; Black or African-American approximately 13 percent; Asian approximately 6 percent; multiracial and other approximately 3 percent [kff-race-ethnicity-acs-2024]. Linguistic composition: English is the de facto national language with no official federal designation; Spanish is the second most spoken language; approximately 8 percent of the population has limited English proficiency. Religious composition: per the 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study by Pew Research Center, approximately 62 percent identify as Christian (Protestant approximately 45 percent, Catholic approximately 20 percent, other Christian approximately 7 percent); approximately 28 percent identify as religiously unaffiliated ('nones'); Muslim, Jewish, Buddhist, and Hindu communities each account for approximately 1-3 percent [pew-religious-landscape-2024]. CLEAVAGE GEOMETRY: The principal fault lines in U.S. society are REINFORCING, not cross-cutting: racial identity, educational attainment, geographic location (urban vs. rural/exurban), and partisan affiliation have progressively stacked along the same social divides over the past two decades — white non-college rural voters align overwhelmingly Republican; college-educated urban voters align increasingly Democratic; racial minority communities align predominantly Democratic. This stacking means political conflict carries racial, educational, and geographic dimensions simultaneously, creating a more explosive social geometry than cross-cutting cleavages would produce [pew-trust-government-2025][vdem-democracy-report-2026].
composition.fr: Composition ethnique et raciale (tabulation KFF de l'American Community Survey (ACS), 2024) : Blanc non hispanique ~59 %; Hispanique ou Latino ~19 %; Noir ou Afro-Américain ~13 %; Asiatique ~6 %; multiracial et autre ~3 % [kff-race-ethnicity-acs-2024]. Composition religieuse : selon la 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study du Pew Research Center, environ 62 % se déclarent chrétiens (protestants ~45 %, catholiques ~20 %, autres chrétiens ~7 %); environ 28 % se déclarent sans affiliation religieuse ('nones') [pew-religious-landscape-2024]. GÉOMÉTRIE DES CLIVAGES : Les principales lignes de fracture sont RENFORÇANTES, non transversales : l'identité raciale, le niveau d'instruction, la localisation géographique et l'affiliation partisane se sont progressivement empilés le long des mêmes fractures sociales, créant une géométrie sociale plus explosive que des clivages transversaux ne le feraient [pew-trust-government-2025][vdem-democracy-report-2026].

religion.en: (a) Composition: approximately 62 percent Christian, 28 percent unaffiliated, and the remainder distributed across Jewish (~2%), Muslim (~1%), Buddhist (~1%), Hindu (~1%), and other faiths, per the 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study: Executive Summary published by Pew Research Center (2025); the principal religious fault line is between practicing Christians — particularly evangelical Protestants concentrated in the South and exurban areas — and the 'nones', who are disproportionately urban, younger, and college-educated [pew-religious-landscape-2024]. Source reliability: the Pew 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study is methodologically rigorous (large nationally representative sample) but relies on self-identification and may overcount nominal affiliates; no official government count of religion exists in the United States; the Association of Religion Data Archives (ARDA) — U.S. Religion Surveys and Data portal aggregates over 900 independent academic surveys that corroborate the Pew direction of trend (declining Christian share, rising 'nones') across multiple methodologies [arda-us-religion][pew-religious-landscape-2024]. (b) Lived texture: Indigenous spiritual practices persist among Native American and Alaska Native communities and are legally protected under the American Indian Religious Freedom Act; Pentecostal and charismatic practice is significant within the nominally Protestant count; syncretism between Catholic and indigenous practice is present in Latino communities. (c) Political salience: HIGH and rising. Evangelical Protestant churches serve as organisational infrastructure for Republican political mobilisation, particularly in the South and Midwest; the Supreme Court has progressively expanded religious liberty exemptions from neutral laws of general applicability in rulings from 2020-2025; religious identity is a stronger predictor of partisan affiliation and voting behaviour than at any point in recent polling history [pew-trust-government-2025].
religion.fr: (a) Composition : environ 62 % chrétiens, 28 % sans affiliation, le reste distribué entre juifs (~2 %), musulmans (~1 %), bouddhistes (~1 %), hindous (~1 %) et autres, selon la 2023-24 Religious Landscape Study: Executive Summary du Pew Research Center (2025); la principale ligne de fracture religieuse oppose les chrétiens pratiquants — en particulier les protestants évangéliques — aux 'nones', qui sont disproportionnément urbains, jeunes et diplômés universitaires [pew-religious-landscape-2024]. Fiabilité de la source : l'étude Pew est méthodologiquement rigoureuse mais repose sur l'auto-identification; aucun recensement officiel de la religion n'existe aux États-Unis; le portail ARDA (Association of Religion Data Archives) agrège plus de 900 enquêtes académiques indépendantes qui corroborent la direction de la tendance Pew [arda-us-religion][pew-religious-landscape-2024]. (c) Saillance politique : ÉLEVÉE et en hausse. Les Églises protestantes évangéliques servent d'infrastructure organisationnelle pour la mobilisation politique républicaine; l'identité religieuse est un prédicteur plus fort de l'affiliation partisane et du comportement électoral qu'à n'importe quel moment de l'histoire récente des sondages [pew-trust-government-2025].

cohesion.reliabilityFlag: PARTISAN-SORTED — headline aggregate is a systematically distorted artefact; cohort breakdowns are the analytically valid instrument
cohesion.en: Social trust data for the United States must be interpreted under the partisan-sorted reliability flag: respondents answer honestly, but responses track which party holds the government rather than stable underlying trust levels; the headline aggregate is a systematically distorted artefact and cohort breakdowns are the analytically valid instrument. Primary instruments: Pew Research Center — Public Trust in Government: 1958-2025 and Gallup — U.S. Trust in Government Depends Upon Party Control. Cohort breakdowns (Pew, late 2025 data): only 17 percent of Americans overall say they trust the federal government to do what is right 'just about always' or 'most of the time'; partisan cohort split: only 9 percent of Democrats and Democratic-leaning independents trust the federal government — the lowest Pew has ever recorded for this cohort; 26 percent of Republicans and Republican-leaning independents report trust, on par with GOP views during the first Trump administration [pew-trust-government-2025]. Gallup (2025 data): 45 percent of U.S. adults have a 'great deal or fair amount' of trust in the federal government to handle international problems; 38 percent trust it to handle domestic problems; trust in the three branches ranges from 32 percent for Congress to 49 percent for the judiciary; 53 percent of adults — by one point the lowest Gallup has measured — trust the American people themselves to make judgments under the democratic system [gallup-trust-2025]. The V-Dem Liberal Democracy Index decline of 24 percent in 2025, the Freedom House score drop to 81, and the Pew finding that 69 percent of Americans are dissatisfied with the way democracy is working (Democrats 86 percent dissatisfied, Republicans 51 percent dissatisfied) collectively indicate a society under significant cohesion stress [vdem-democracy-report-2026][freedom-house-2026][pew-democracy-decline-2026].
cohesion.fr: Les données de confiance sociale doivent être interprétées sous le drapeau de fiabilité 'partisan-sorted' : les répondants répondent honnêtement, mais les réponses reflètent le parti qui contrôle le gouvernement plutôt que des niveaux de confiance stables. Ventilations par cohorte partisane (Pew, fin 2025) : seulement 17 % des Américains font confiance au gouvernement fédéral 'presque toujours ou la plupart du temps'; division par cohorte : seulement 9 % des Démocrates et des indépendants à tendance démocrate — le niveau le plus bas jamais enregistré par Pew pour cette cohorte; 26 % des Républicains et des indépendants à tendance républicaine déclarent faire confiance [pew-trust-government-2025]. Gallup (2025) : 45 % des adultes américains font 'beaucoup ou assez' confiance au gouvernement fédéral pour gérer les problèmes internationaux; 38 % pour les problèmes nationaux; 53 % font confiance au peuple américain lui-même — le niveau le plus bas jamais mesuré par Gallup [gallup-trust-2025]. Le déclin de 24 % de l'Indice V-Dem LDI en 2025, la chute du score Freedom House à 81, et le constat que 69 % des Américains sont insatisfaits du fonctionnement de la démocratie indiquent collectivement une société sous un stress de cohésion significatif [vdem-democracy-report-2026][freedom-house-2026][pew-democracy-decline-2026].

internal.en: The United States does not face an active domestic insurgency or civil war; territorial control is full across all 50 states and the District of Columbia [doi-insular-affairs]. The principal domestic security threats as assessed in the U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Homeland Threat Assessment 2025 are: (1) domestic violent extremism — primarily racially or ethnically motivated violent extremism (RMVE) and anti-government/anti-authority violent extremism; (2) foreign terrorist organisations — including Islamic State (IS) and al-Qaeda affiliated actors; (3) transnational criminal organisations — primarily Mexican cartels conducting fentanyl trafficking and human smuggling; (4) state-sponsored cyber threats from China, Russia, Iran, and North Korea against critical infrastructure [dhs-hta-2025]. Protest activity: the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED) United States and Canada Overview: July 2026 documents that protest activity has been sustained and largely peaceful as of July 2026; the No Kings III protests on 28 March 2026 constituted the largest single-day mobilisation of demonstrations in recent years [acled-usa-july-2026]. Military spending: Stockholm International Peace Research Institute (SIPRI) Trends in World Military Expenditure, 2025 documents U.S. military spending at $954 billion in 2025 — a decrease of 7.5 percent in real terms from 2024, though still by far the largest in the world and approximately 37 percent of global military spending [sipri-milex-2025].
internal.fr: Les États-Unis ne font pas face à une insurrection intérieure active; le contrôle territorial est total sur les 50 États et le District de Columbia [doi-insular-affairs]. Les principales menaces selon le U.S. Department of Homeland Security (DHS) Homeland Threat Assessment 2025 sont : (1) l'extrémisme violent intérieur — principalement motivé par des considérations raciales ou anti-gouvernementales; (2) les organisations terroristes étrangères; (3) les organisations criminelles transnationales — principalement les cartels mexicains conduisant le trafic de fentanyl; (4) les cybermenaces parrainées par des États (Chine, Russie, Iran, Corée du Nord) contre les infrastructures critiques [dhs-hta-2025]. Les manifestations No Kings III du 28 mars 2026 ont constitué la plus grande mobilisation en un seul jour ces dernières années selon le Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project (ACLED) [acled-usa-july-2026]. Les dépenses militaires américaines s'élevaient à 954 milliards de dollars en 2025 selon le SIPRI, représentant environ 37 % des dépenses militaires mondiales [sipri-milex-2025].

diplomacy.en: The United States maintains the world's most extensive treaty alliance network and multilateral membership portfolio, documented in Treaties in Force: A List of Treaties and Other International Agreements of the United States published by the U.S. Department of State as of 1 January 2025. Core defence architecture: North Atlantic Treaty Organization (NATO) founding member under the North Atlantic Treaty (1949), committing to collective defence under Article 5; mutual defence treaties in force with Japan (Treaty of Mutual Cooperation and Security, 1960), South Korea (Mutual Defense Treaty, 1954), Australia (ANZUS, 1951), and the Philippines (Mutual Defense Treaty, 1951) [state-dept-treaties-in-force-2025]. Key bilateral relationships: the U.S.-Canada relationship is under significant strain in 2025-2026 following tariff escalation; U.S.-China relations are defined by strategic competition across technology, trade, and Taiwan; U.S.-Israel relations remain a central axis of Middle East policy. The International Crisis Group (ICG) Ten Conflicts to Watch in 2026 identifies the U.S. posture toward Iran — shaped by the 2025 U.S.-Israel military operation against Iran's nuclear infrastructure — as a primary geopolitical risk driver with global energy-price ramifications [icg-conflicts-watch-2026]. Multilateral memberships: the United States is a permanent member of the United Nations (UN) Security Council, a Group of Seven (G7) and Group of Twenty (G20) member, an IMF and World Bank shareholder (largest), and a World Trade Organization (WTO) member; it has withdrawn from the Paris Agreement and the World Health Organization (WHO) under the current administration [state-dept-treaties-in-force-2025]. The 2025 Trade Policy Agenda documents an assertive, America-first trade policy posture using tariffs as leverage [ustr-trade-policy-2025].
diplomacy.fr: Les États-Unis maintiennent le réseau d'alliances de traités le plus étendu au monde, documenté dans les Treaties in Force du Département d'État américain au 1er janvier 2025. Architecture de défense centrale : membre fondateur de l'Organisation du traité de l'Atlantique Nord (OTAN) sous le Traité de l'Atlantique Nord (1949); traités de défense mutuelle en vigueur avec le Japon (1960), la Corée du Sud (1954), l'Australie (ANZUS, 1951), et les Philippines (1951) [state-dept-treaties-in-force-2025]. Le Ten Conflicts to Watch in 2026 du International Crisis Group (ICG) identifie la posture américaine vis-à-vis de l'Iran — façonnée par l'opération militaire États-Unis-Israël de 2025 contre l'infrastructure nucléaire iranienne — comme un moteur de risque géopolitique primaire [icg-conflicts-watch-2026]. Adhésions multilatérales : membre permanent du Conseil de sécurité des Nations Unies (ONU), membre du Groupe des Sept (G7) et du Groupe des Vingt (G20); les États-Unis se sont retirés de l'Accord de Paris et de l'Organisation mondiale de la santé (OMS) sous l'administration actuelle [state-dept-treaties-in-force-2025].

title.fr: Falaise budgétaire et détérioration de la crédibilité de la dette

trigger.en: Failure to pass budget legislation or continuing resolution before FY 2026 end (30 September 2026) produces government shutdown; alternatively, passage of reconciliation legislation adds materially to deficit without offsetting revenue, triggering bond-market repricing and potential second sovereign downgrade
trigger.fr: L'échec à adopter une législation budgétaire ou une résolution de poursuite avant la fin de l'EF 2026 (30 septembre 2026) produit une paralysie gouvernementale (government shutdown); alternativement, l'adoption d'une législation de réconciliation alourdit matériellement le déficit, déclenchant une réévaluation du marché obligataire et un potentiel second déclassement souverain

leadingIndicators.fr: Écart de rendement des obligations du Trésor à 10 ans par rapport aux pairs; évaluation du CBO du paquet de réconciliation; comptage des voix à la Chambre; annonces de surveillance des notes par Moody's ou Fitch
